facts.statement: Paratomistoma is an extinct genus containing only one species, classified as a gavialoid crocodylian.
facts.quote: Paratomistoma (meaning "next to or near Tomistoma") is an extinct monospecific genus of gavialoid crocodylian.

facts.statement: Paratomistoma was named in 2000 by paleontologists Christopher Brochu and Philip Gingerich.
facts.quote: Paratomistoma was named in 2000 by Christopher Brochu and Philip Gingerich

facts.statement: The type species is P. courti, named in honor of Nicholas Court, the discoverer of the holotype specimen.
facts.quote: the type species is P. courti in honor of Nicholas Court, who found CGM 42188.

facts.statement: Despite being unfused, the holotype skull is considered to represent a morphologically mature individual.
facts.quote: The skull is unfused but considered morphologically mature.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis identified Paratomistoma as a derived member of the subfamily Tomistominae, closely related to the false gharial.
facts.quote: They performed a phylogenetic analysis and found Paratomistoma to be a derived member of Tomistominae, related to the false gharial.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Paratomistoma may have lived in marine or coastal environments.
facts.quote: It may have been a marine or coastal crocodilian.

facts.statement: Recent molecular studies indicate that Tomistominae, including Paratomistoma, belong to the family Gavialidae rather than being crocodiles.
facts.quote: However, recent molecular studies using DNA sequencing have consistently indicated that the false gharial (Tomistoma) (and by inference other related extinct forms in Tomistominae) actually belong to Gavialoidea (and Gavialidae).

facts.statement: Paratomistoma lived during the Bartonian stage of the Middle Eocene, between 41.03 and 37.71 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Bartonian to Bartonian (41.03 to 37.71 million years ago)

facts.statement: Paratomistoma belongs to the parent group Tomistominae.
Paratomistoma is classified within the family Gavialidae.
